rationale: B wins because it finds one sharper structural story A mostly misses: “Perplexity is now paid twice on the same answer — and the publisher gets a slice of one payment.” That is a real reported angle if the terms support it, and B is honest enough to say it dies if referral revenue is shared. A is strong, especially “Perplexity will pay publishers it cites. It won't say how much,” but it plays the safer obvious board and wrongly dismisses the query-volume data angle as having no journalist shape when B shows exactly how a media-business data reporter could work it.
gaps_in_A: “Hundreds of millions of queries a month: the scale of Perplexity's new ad economy” is refused as “no_journalist_shape,” but that is too quick; a media-business/data reporter could use the query claim plus undisclosed payout terms as the accountability math story.

“Perplexity turns its answer engine into a checkout and takes a referral fee on every sale” overstates the facts with “on every sale”; the update says Perplexity earns a referral fee, not necessarily on every transaction.
The funding angle says the launch is “the first concrete monetization signal since the raise,” which is plausible but not provided. That needs attribution or softer wording.
It misses the cleanest tension between the two revenue streams: publishers share ad revenue, while referral-fee sharing is not disclosed.
gaps_in_B: “Perplexity starts paying publishers it was being sued over” is too loose. The update says legal threats, not lawsuits, and no publisher payout is confirmed yet.

“paid twice on the same answer” is a useful contrarian hypothesis, but it leans on inference. B correctly caveats it, but the headline itself is stronger than the supplied facts allow until referral revenue treatment is confirmed.

“search-referral decline for publishers” appears in the data angle without being in the update. It is beat context, not a supplied fact, but it should be framed as reporter context, not evidence from the company update.
The valuation angle repeats “the first visible consumer-revenue mechanisms” without proving there were no prior visible mechanisms. It is a small grounding wobble.
